items.prompt: From one IP, a user signs in successfully 20 times within fifteen minutes. What happens on the 21st attempt, made with the correct password?
items.answer: It is refused with 429, because successes count toward the limit too
distractors: It succeeds, because only failed password checks add to the count
It succeeds, and the counter for that IP starts again from zero
It is refused with 401 until the full fifteen-minute window has closed
items.explanation: entry.count++ runs before the password is compared and nothing resets it on success, so the 21st attempt in the window hits count >= 20 and gets 429 with Retry-After 900.

items.prompt: The login limiter already tracks 1000 unexpired IP entries. A legitimate user tries to sign in from a new IP for the first time. What happens?
items.answer: They get 429 on their very first attempt from that address
distractors: The oldest tracked IP is evicted and the new attempt is checked
Their attempt is checked, but it is not recorded in the map
They get 503, as the limiter treats a full table as an outage
items.explanation: The guard refuses when the key is untracked and attempts.size >= 1000. Expired entries are swept first, but with 1000 live entries a new address is refused outright, which is the cost the practice exercise asks you to name.

items.prompt: A login body carries a password of 100 UTF-8 bytes. What does the login handler do with it?
items.answer: It counts the attempt, then fails validation with a 400 response
distractors: It truncates the password to 72 bytes and compares it with bcrypt
It rejects it with 400 before the attempt is added to the counter
It returns 401, the same response that a wrong password gets
items.explanation: entry.count++ and attempts.set run before loginInput.parse, and loginInput refuses passwords over 72 UTF-8 bytes; the ZodError maps to 400. Nothing is truncated.

items.prompt: Ten minutes after signing in, an OWNER of Cedar is demoted to MEMBER. Their token is still valid. They now POST a new Cedar project. What happens?
items.answer: 403, since the role comes from the membership row on each request
distractors: 201, because the token still carries the OWNER role it was issued with
401, and the user has to sign in again to get a fresh token
201 until the token expires, then 403 on the first call after that
items.explanation: The token holds only the subject. attachTenantContext reads the membership for (userId, x-org-id) on every request, so the new MEMBER role reaches requireManager, which refuses project changes with 403.

items.prompt: A MEMBER of Maple sends DELETE for a Maple task, with the task's current version in a JSON body. What happens?
items.answer: The task is deleted and a DELETE audit event is written with it
distractors: 403, because deleting anything needs an owner or an administrator
The task is deleted, but deletes by members are left out of the audit
403 unless the member is the user who originally created the task
items.explanation: deleteTask in the service does not call requireManager (members can manage tasks), and removeTask writes the audit row in the same transaction as the delete, whatever the role.

items.prompt: An admin deletes a project with an outdated version number, and the project still has two tasks. Which error comes back?
items.answer: 409 saying the record changed; the version is checked first
distractors: 409 asking for its tasks to be deleted before the project itself
400, since a stale version fails the request schema check
200; the tasks are removed together with the project
items.explanation: deleteMany matches nothing, then the code re-reads the project and throws the stale-record conflict when row.version !== expected, before it reaches the tasks message. The schema only checks that version is a positive integer.

items.prompt: A Cedar admin sends PUT for a project id that exists only in Maple, with x-org-id set to Cedar and version 1. What is the response?
items.answer: 404, because the follow-up lookup is scoped to Cedar
distractors: 409, because the conditional update matched zero rows
200, and the Maple project is renamed by the update
403, because that id belongs to another organization
items.explanation: updateMany matches zero rows, and before reporting a conflict the code calls projectIn with Cedar, which finds nothing and throws 404. The foreign row is never touched.

items.prompt: A user searches projects for 50%_off. Which string does the repository hand to Prisma's contains filter?
items.answer: 50\%\_off, so both characters match as literal text
distractors: 50%_off unchanged, since the query is parameterized
50off, with both wildcard characters stripped out
50%%__off, with each wildcard character doubled
items.explanation: literal() prefixes every backslash, percent and underscore with a backslash. Parameterization stops SQL injection but would still let % and _ act as LIKE wildcards.

items.prompt: GET /api/projects?q=api&sort=name reaches the project list service. What happens?
items.answer: 400, as the strict list schema refuses the unknown sort key
distractors: 200, with sort ignored and the default ordering applied instead
200, with the projects sorted by name as requested
500, since the unknown key reaches the Prisma query
items.explanation: listInput is a strict zod object with only q and page, so parse throws a ZodError for sort and the error handler maps it to 400.

items.prompt: A client sends PUT /api/projects/p1?force=true with a valid JSON body and the current version. What happens?
items.answer: It is rejected with 400 because mutation routes refuse query strings
distractors: It is accepted; force is ignored and the update runs as usual
It is accepted, and force skips the version check for this save
It is accepted, but force is recorded in the audit event metadata field
items.explanation: The router guard refuses any non-GET request that has query parameters, before the body or version is read.

items.prompt: How does the backend's CORS check treat a request from curl that sends no Origin header at all?
items.answer: It lets it through; only a different Origin is refused
distractors: It refuses it with 403 like any unrecognized origin
It lets it through only for GET requests and the health check
It refuses it unless it targets the /api/auth routes
items.explanation: The origin callback raises the 403 AppError only when origin is set and differs from frontendOrigin. With no Origin there is nothing to compare, so the request continues to authentication as normal.

items.prompt: A client POSTs a project whose JSON body is 40 KB, almost all of it description text. What status does the API return?
items.answer: 413, as the JSON parser caps request bodies at 32 KiB
distractors: 400, as description is capped at 2000 characters
201, since the description field has no length cap
500, since the parser error has no mapped status
items.explanation: express.json({ limit: "32kb" }) rejects the body before any route runs, and errorHandler maps entity.too.large to 413. The 2000-character schema limit is never reached.

items.front: Why does an x-org-id header alone grant nothing in this API?
items.back: It is only a selection. attachTenantContext validates its format (400 if malformed), then looks up the membership for the verified token user and that organization; no membership means 403. The role used for policy comes from that membership row, not from the token or the body.

items.front: How does the repository tell a stale project update apart from a missing project?
items.back: updateMany matches id, organization and expected version. If the count is not 1 it re-reads the project scoped to the organization: not found gives 404, found gives the 409 conflict. The accepted update and its audit insert share one transaction.

items.front: What does the Task composite foreign key (projectId, organizationId) -> Project(id, organizationId) protect?
items.back: The database itself refuses a task that names one organization while pointing at another organization's project, so tenant consistency does not rest on query conventions alone. onDelete: Restrict also means projects are never cascaded away with their tasks.

items.front: Parameterized SQL and wildcard escaping: which problem does each solve?
items.back: Parameterization keeps user text from being executed as SQL (injection). Escaping % and _ (and the backslash) keeps that text from acting as LIKE wildcards, so a search for 100% matches the literal characters. You need both.
